newsitem.title: PANAMA: Latin leaders eye anti-drug center in Panama.
newsitem.headline: Latin leaders eye anti-drug center in Panama.

text.p: Anti-drug leaders from Colombia, Mexico, Venezuela and Bolivia will visit a U.S. military base in Panama later this month to see how a proposed international anti-drug centre would function, officials said Thursday.

The Latin American officials will visit Howard Air Force Base Sept. 16-18 to assess its possible use as a regional base to coordinate the war against drug trafficking, Foreign Minister Ricardo Arias told a news conference.

President Ernesto Perez Balladares has said that Panama is willing to allow the United States to keep Howard Air Force Base in Panama at no cost and use it as an international drug fighting centre. The base is due to be turned over to Panamanian control in the year 2000 according to Panama Canal treaties.
